text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Competition heightens in the banking industry with bigger banks undercutting smaller ones in interest rates charges.
- World price of Nigeria's Bonny Light crude oil has bounced back to above $20 a barrel, because of rising demand.
- Elf Nigeria Petroleum oil company will increase its oil and condensate production in Nigeria by 18,000 barrels per day when its Obite gas project comes on stream in 1999.
- Seven countries have indicated interest in participating in the development of Nigeria's solid minerals, officials say.
- The national electricity grid is overloaded, fuelling fear of an imminent nationwide blackout.
- The central bank mopped up a total of 11.59 billion naira from circulation at the weekend.
- Nigeria is to reopen its customs post in Brussels, Belgium, says the customs chief Brigadier-General Samuel Ango.
- Central bank may issue licences to new banks in October, after riding the system of distressed financial institutions, to meet growing investor interest.
- The big four banks in the country are planning to establish a company for sorting out currency notes.
- Nigerian stock exchange is considering placing an embargo on licensing new stock brokers in order to curb the proliferation of operators in the capital markets.
- Banks affected by a recent ultimatum to refund forex they received in contravention of rules governing the foreign exchange market are in a fix on how to meet the deadline.

- Deputy managing director of Ashaka Cement Company James Cook, urges Nigerian military government to invite new British Prime Minister Tony Blair to visit the country, saying this will give him first hand information on Nigeria's crisis.
